author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Rhode Island held its principal September 11 remembrance Friday at the Rhode Island Veterans Memorial Cemetery in Exeter, 25 years after the attacks, NBC 10 reported. Bells sounded for each of the four hijacked flights as attendees gathered at the cemetery's Wall of Honor.

Rhode Island State Police Colonel Darnell Weaver read the names of nine Rhode Islanders who were killed on September 11, 2001. The ceremony also recognized nine service members from the state who died in wars that followed the attacks. Gold Star families placed a wreath in remembrance, joining veterans, public officials, first responders and community members.

The Exeter observance was among ceremonies across the state, but its setting connected the civilian toll of the attacks with the military service and losses that followed. The anniversary gave families and residents a formal space to remember individual lives while teaching a generation born after 2001 why the day remains central to public memory. Organizers framed the event around service, sacrifice and continued support for families carrying those losses.
dek: Bells marked the four hijacked flights as state leaders and Gold Star families remembered Rhode Islanders killed in the attacks and later wars.
headline: Rhode Island honors September 11 victims at Exeter ceremony
